newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ramos urges APEC businessmen to "Go Go Go".
newsitem.headline: Ramos urges APEC businessmen to "Go Go Go".

text.p: Urging businessmen to "Go Go Go", Philippine President Fidel Ramos on Friday appealed for action to forge the world's largest free trade and investment zone circling the Pacific Rim.

In rousing messages to businessmen and government ministers at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum, Ramos said the private sector was key to APEC's vision of a borderless economy embracing half the world's people by 2020.
"Now we move into the action phase," Ramos said at the start of a two-day meeting of ministers which kicked off to the strains of "Land of Hope and Glory".
Outside the hall riot police charged a group of more than 100 students demonstrating against APEC in the latest of a series of protests this past week.
The students waved banners saying "No to APEC" before being scattered by the baton-wielding police.
Hundreds of demonstrators have been marching in this capital to denounce APEC's pro-business vision of a single trading bloc for goods, services and technology.
A coalition of trade unionists, leftist activists and Roman Catholic clergy argue that free movement of capital in the region will benefit rich nations at the expense of poor.
The ministers are polishing a blueprint for open trade to be endorsed by leaders of 18 APEC economies at a summit on Monday in Subic Bay north of Manila.
Ramos, who is transforming the Philippines from sick man of Asia to an emerging "tiger" economy, earlier told an Asia-Pacific Business Forum that open trade benefited everyone.
"The APEC vision is about improving people's lives," Ramos said.
"Let's go for it! Go Go Go!"
APEC ministers are stitching together free-market initiatives of individual members of the informal APEC grouping developed since the second APEC summit in Indonesia two years ago.
Ramos told the businessmen that growth and prosperity were created by "economies driven by the energy and enterprise of the private sector".

In Indonesia, APEC members agreed to create a seamless trading bloc without tariffs or government red-tape. They set a timetable of 2010 for developed nations to fully open their markets and 2020 for developing economies.
Ramos called for APEC nations to strengthen economic and technical cooperation.
He urged members to stabilise financial markets, develop infrastructure, ensure environmentally sustainable growth and strengthen the role of small- and medium-sized enterprises.
Leftist groups fear that small businessmen and craftsmen will be pushed aside by transnational corporations, and poor countries will turn into manufacturing sweatshops.

This year's annual APEC summit comes at a time of looming trouble for APEC's most dynamic economies, particularly the Asian tigers whose economies have been hit by falling prices for their exports and weakness in the Japanese currency.
Sceptics say these economies, slowing after years of double-digit growth, are more likely to retreat behind barriers than expose themselves to further competition by tearing down obstacles to trade.
Nevertheless, in an encouraging sign of cooperation, this year's summit looks set to back a U.S. plan to axe tariffs on the global trade in computers and parts worth $1.8 trillion.

APEC groups Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand and the United States.

APEC officials dashed hopes of countries such as Russia, India, Vietnam and Peru of speedy membership by saying no one else would be admitted until 1988 at the earliest when the APEC summit will be in Kuala Lumpur. The 1997 summit will be in Vancouver.
